title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Free-Time Records per Container and Leg
content:
## Principle

Demurrage and Detention Free Time is held record by record. Every container on every leg billed to a customer has a free-time record of its own, and the number of records one customer can have is unlimited.

A record is identified by three things together: the booking, the container number and the direction, import or export. For any one combination of those three there is never more than one record. Should the same container travel again on another booking, that booking has its own record for it.

## Basis of the judgement

Whether a record already exists is read from the company's own free-time records, never from the customer's account of them, and it is tested before any record is opened. An existing record for the same booking, container and direction stands in the way of a second one whether it shows free time running, charges accruing, clock stopped, invoiced or settled. A record that shows cancelled is not among those states.

## Input, judgement, output

| Input: records already held for the same booking, container and direction | Judgement | Output |
|---|---|---|
| none | the combination is new | one record is opened |
| one, free time running | the combination is already held | no second record |
| one, settled | the combination is already held | no second record |
| one, cancelled only | a cancelled record is not one of the blocking states | the duplicate test does not stand in the way |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- One container discharged under booking A and later loaded for export under booking A has two records, one per direction.
- The same container later moving under booking B receives its own records under booking B; the records under booking A are untouched.
- A forwarder with four hundred containers in motion holds four hundred or more records; the count is never capped.
